findings: In a sandbox the integration can create test card charges through Dashboard or test-key API. Both captures list card numbers, tokens and PaymentMethods for rule-dependent highest, always-blocked highest and elevated outcomes. The elevated rows specify signals but no queue transition.

Rule testing before addition/update searches historical live-mode payments. Operators inspect matching transactions and aggregate volume/count outcomes. Allow-rule Overrides are previously Radar-blocked payments that would be allowed under the proposed rule.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/testing, source-stripe-radar-testing should distinguish sandbox payment simulation from a proposed rule's historical backtest. In both captures the integration creates sandbox test card charges through Dashboard or the create-charge API with a test key. The three card/token/PaymentMethod rows produce rule-dependent highest risk, highest risk always blocked, and elevated risk. The legacy highest-risk rule is an example of why the first path may be blocked and elevated does not by itself promise a default queue action (old raw lines 8-32 and new raw lines 9-33). November also documents using those test card numbers with the Payment Evaluation API to force fraudulent_payment risk levels and adding SEPA and ACH Direct Debit inputs that simulate a Radar block in a sandbox (new raw line 9 and new raw lines 35-49). Before adding or updating a rule, Stripe searches matching historical live-mode payments and the operator can inspect the list and counts/volume for disputes or warnings, refunds, blocked or issuer-failed, and succeeded. Allow backtests add potential Overrides for payments previously blocked by Radar (old raw lines 34-45 and new raw lines 51-62). The existing May-based summary retains these categories but overstates rule-dependent blocking and elevated review, lacks the new sandbox routes, and attributes a six-month window where these two captures give no duration.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/testing, update source-stripe-radar-testing. The 2026-11-07 capture substantively adds the sandbox card-to-Payment Evaluation API route for the fraudulent_payment signal and the separate simulated SEPA and ACH Direct Debit blocks (old raw lines 8-16 and new raw lines 9-17, old raw lines 26-36 and new raw lines 27-53). These tests say nothing about an evaluation's live processor outcome. Table alignment, screenshot location and minor Allow guidance phrasing are presentational; the November note retains the trade-off, the inability to know what previously blocked charges would have done, and the 3DS challenge and early-warning qualifications (old raw lines 45-61 and new raw lines 62-77). Preserve the dated May card scenarios, historical live-payment context and rule-dependent block/elevated descriptions (old raw lines 8-45 and new raw lines 9-62). The six-month wording comes from the separately captured November Review rules passage (raw/stripe-radar-rules-2026-11-07.md:270-278). Keep both raw links, the reciprocal stripe-radar, provider index and company routes, and connect the sandbox evaluation subsection to source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor and the historical backtest subsection to source-stripe-radar-rules.
